speaker: fox
text: "I've got two cups and one important question. Tea, or the terrible cocoa I keep trying to improve?"

speaker: narrator
text: 'One cup has a chip in the handle. The other has a crooked flower painted on it.'

speaker: fox
text: "That flower was meant to be a fox. You can be kind about it, but please don't lie."

speaker: fox
text: "Brave. I mean about the cocoa. The flower is excellent company."

speaker: narrator
text: 'She moves the chipped cup to her own place.'

speaker: fox
text: "It suits your hand, doesn't it? I keep forgetting that a thing can be chipped and still be exactly right."

speaker: narrator
text: "She puts the cocoa away and does not look disappointed."

speaker: narrator
text: `Below the house, ${word} catches against the rim instead of sinking.`

speaker: owl
text: "Wait. I wrote that word in my notebook this morning. Before you brought it down here."

speaker: narrator
text: "He lays the open notebook down beside the rim. The letters match."

speaker: narrator
text: "The same letters are already scratched into the stone beside the rim. The scratches are old."

speaker: fox
text: "I could call this a coincidence, friend. I would like that word to be some help. It is not."

speaker: narrator
text: "The word sinks. Its reflection stays on the surface one moment longer."

speaker: narrator
text: 'You write down what happened by the rim: the same word, already there before you offered it. You put the date beneath it.'

speaker: fox
text: "I would like to fold that page away, friend. I can hear myself reaching for another comforting explanation."

speaker: fox
text: "But you were there too. Shall we tell the household what we saw, or keep the account between us while we look into it?"

speaker: narrator
text: 'You bring the account to the shared table. Those who read it add their initials beneath the date.'

speaker: fox
text: "I will tell them what happened. I will say I do not know why. You can stop me if I start making it sound safer than it is."

speaker: narrator
text: 'You fold the dated account and keep it with you. Ember leaves the outside blank.'

speaker: fox
text: "Between us, then. When you want someone else to read it, you can be the one to open it."

speaker: narrator
text: `Ember sets ${cupName} at your place. ${cup === 'flower' ? "She has been working on the cocoa recipe again." : "She remembered that you asked for tea."}`

speaker: pangolin
text: "Supper. Now. The empty place at the table can wait. The rest of us have stomachs."

speaker: narrator
text: "She sets the covered dish aside on the floor and serves everyone from the ordinary pot."

speaker: fox
text: "I spent the whole afternoon keeping a place warm for someone who has not come. Your drink went cold while I did it. That is ridiculous of me, friend."

speaker: narrator
text: `The empty cup is moved aside. Fresh ${cup ? drink : 'tea'} goes in ${cup ? cupName : 'yours'}.`

speaker: rabbit
text: 'Is it safe?'

speaker: pangolin
text: "It is soup. I made it myself. Ask me about the house after you have eaten."

speaker: fox
text: "The tea is safe. I cannot promise you anything else tonight."

speaker: narrator
text: "For a while the room sounds like an ordinary supper, not like a room listening for something."

speaker: narrator
text: 'The dated account lies between the dishes, its row of initials visible.'

speaker: fox
text: "You asked us to tell everyone. If anyone has seen something else, this is a good place to say it."

speaker: narrator
text: 'The folded account is still in your pocket. Ember glances toward you, then leaves it for you to bring up.'

speaker: narrator
text: "Under the table, the low hum below the floor slips out of rhythm. Nobody hurries to set it right."

speaker: wombat
text: "I always read this line on the old plan as a brace. Look which way it points."

speaker: narrator
text: "Warren turns a drawing of the foundations so the doorway faces you."

speaker: narrator
text: "A loose plan lies under the oldest hearthstone. Its arrows point in toward the house, not away from it."

speaker: tarsier
text: "My watch keeps the house in sight all night. Nobody ever told me who I am watching for."

speaker: fox
text: "All that work to keep something out. Or maybe, friend, that is only what we wanted the drawing to mean."

speaker: owl
text: "I wrote \"defense\" beside this mark in the old book. The book never used that word. I did."

speaker: narrator
text: "Someone has written SAFE in the margin. The handwriting is much newer than the plan."

speaker: narrator
text: "A line goes through the reassuring word. Nobody writes a new one under it. It is the first answer anyone has crossed out."

speaker: narrator
text: 'The arrows on the old plan all point inward. Beside the drawing, you set a lamp and a small latch.'

speaker: wombat
text: "I can mark the road beyond the gate. Or fit this latch to a door we already have, and ask everyone to knock. Which shall I start with?"

speaker: fox
text: "We could mark the road beyond the gate, friend. Or put this latch on a door we already have, and ask everyone to knock. Which would help you tonight?"

speaker: narrator
text: 'Neither a lamp nor a latch can promise to stop what is below the house. They are things the people here can do for one another now.'

speaker: narrator
text: 'You set the lamp by the gate. Together, you place pale stones along the outward path, as far as the trees.'

speaker: wombat
text: "I will keep these markers clear. I cannot tell you yet what happens past the trees."

speaker: fox
text: "I will keep the lamp filled. I wish that were the same as knowing where the road ends. It is a start."

speaker: narrator
text: 'The latch is fitted to the inside of an existing door. You hang a small sign on the outside: PLEASE KNOCK.'

speaker: wombat
text: "No new room, no clever seal. Just a door that stays shut until you open it. I can ask people to respect that."

speaker: fox
text: "I can promise to knock, friend. Whatever the house does, I can wait until you ask me in."

speaker: axolotl
text: "This is PLUM! He is on his first lap of the tank, worried face and all. He usually stops swimming when I laugh."

speaker: narrator
text: "Axel blows a crooked bubble. PLUM noses it, then turns back to him."

speaker: axolotl
text: "He is old for a fish. I keep forgetting how quickly somebody else can get old."

speaker: narrator
text: "His small hand follows PLUM along the glass, close but never touching."

speaker: narrator
text: `You hold ${cupName}. The ${drink} is warm against your hands.`

speaker: fox
text: "This cup has a chip in it, friend, from the day I dropped it. I still remember who was sitting with me. It would be a poorer cup without that chip."

speaker: narrator
text: "Below the house, a word comes back up out of the dark exactly as it went down. Its reflection does not waver at all."

speaker: fox
text: "Whatever is down there keeps the shape of everything, exactly. I am starting to wonder whether keeping the shape is enough."

speaker: capybara
text: "I wrote this in the ledger: \"I am afraid.\" Three words, complete and accurate."

speaker: narrator
text: "On his ledger, the ink now reads: EVERYTHING IS WELL."

speaker: capybara
text: 'That is tidier. It is also not what I wrote.'

speaker: narrator
text: "On a page beside the hearth, I AM AFRAID changes to EVERYTHING IS WELL. The wet ink shines."

speaker: fox
text: "I watched those letters move with no hand near them. Whatever moved them meant to help, friend. That is what makes this hard."

speaker: fox
text: "We will bring this to the shared table, beside the dated account. You asked us to compare what we saw. We need to keep doing that."

speaker: narrator
text: 'You unfold the dated account beside the ledger. For now, you and Ember compare the pages in private.'

speaker: fox
text: "Keeping the paper is one thing. Remembering what was on it is another. I will remember with you."

speaker: capybara
text: 'I have ink.'

speaker: fox
text: 'Then we will need another pen.'

speaker: narrator
text: "The original sentence is copied onto a loose page and kept away from the ledger."

speaker: capybara
text: "I can leave the house's version on the page. I will not put my name to it."

speaker: fox
text: "We can leave the page alone. We do not have to believe what it says."

speaker: narrator
text: "You remember both sentences. The house kept only one."

speaker: rabbit
text: "I packed seeds. I have not decided to leave. I packed them so that leaving stays something I can still choose."

speaker: narrator
text: "Thyme sets a small tin down beside the garden gate."

speaker: rabbit
text: "Will you keep this between us, or help me tell Ember? I can live with either answer. I cannot live with everyone deciding for me again."

speaker: fox
text: "I used to tell you that you could always leave. I have never walked that road past the trees myself."

speaker: narrator
text: "By the gate, you set a small stone on the path that leads away. A mark you can come back and check."

speaker: rabbit
text: "I saw the lamp you put here, and the pale stones. Someone had thought about leaving before I packed. That helped."

speaker: narrator
text: 'The lamp you chose is still filled. You clear fallen leaves from the pale stones along the outward path.'

speaker: rabbit
text: "People really wait at that PLEASE KNOCK sign you put up. I want that same say over this tin."

speaker: fox
text: "I have learned to wait at your PLEASE KNOCK sign. I want the gate to mean something you can decide, too."

speaker: rabbit
text: "Thank you. A secret is a little room with its own door, and I am the one who opens it."

speaker: fox
text: "Then the stone at the gate stays between us. I will not speak for you."

speaker: fox
text: "I will help. And I will ask you first before I tell anyone else."

speaker: rabbit
text: "Asking first. That would have been a good rule from the very beginning."

speaker: narrator
text: "The stone stays on the outward side of the gate, pointing away from the house."

speaker: fox
text: "I told you I was keeping you safe. That was the promise."

speaker: player
text: 'Did you know what the words were for?'

speaker: fox
text: "I knew enough to tell you. And I did not tell you."

speaker: fox
text: "I knew I was inviting something in. I thought a house full of people who loved each other would teach it to be gentle."

speaker: sloth
text: "I wanted it to come. I called my waiting patience. That word made it easier to watch everyone else wait without knowing why."

speaker: fox
text: "The love in this house was real, friend. It does not excuse what I kept from you."

speaker: narrator
text: 'Through the window, the lamp you chose is lit by the gate.'

speaker: fox
text: "I filled that lamp again. Doing the thing you asked does not make up for the thing I kept from you."

speaker: narrator
text: 'The conversation began with a knock. Ember waited until you opened the latched door.'

speaker: fox
text: "You asked us to wait for permission. I should have understood that before we put up the sign."

speaker: fox
text: "I will tell you the rest. And when I do not know something, I will say so."

speaker: fox
text: "All right. I will keep my distance. Your place in this house does not depend on forgiving me."

speaker: narrator
text: `She moves her chair. ${cup ? cupName[0].toUpperCase() + cupName.slice(1) : 'The cup'} stays within your reach.`

speaker: axolotl
text: "PLUM died. I let him drift down to the bottom of the tank. I should have told someone before I did that."

speaker: narrator
text: "Something with PLUM's worried face swims a full circle of the tank. Then it swims the same circle again, exactly."

speaker: axolotl
text: "The same bite out of his fin. The same little face."

speaker: narrator
text: "Axel laughs once. PLUM always stopped for that. This fish keeps swimming."

speaker: axolotl
text: "Let me have tonight. I am not ready to work this out."

speaker: fox
text: "It kept the part of PLUM it could understand, friend. The shape of him. We will have to show it what it left out."

speaker: narrator
text: "The old cup by the hearth is whole again. Even the line where it was mended has disappeared."

speaker: fox
text: "This is the cup I wanted back, friend. And I cannot remember who was sitting with me when I broke it."

speaker: narrator
text: "She turns the cup over in her paws, looking for the chip."

speaker: fox
text: "The shape is perfect. The chip is gone, and so is the memory of breaking it."

speaker: narrator
text: "The work stops. The last arrangement has not been made yet."

speaker: narrator
text: "A page that said I AM AFRAID now says EVERYTHING IS WELL. The house calls that kindness: keep the sentence, take away the discomfort."

speaker: fox
text: "It learned how to keep us exactly as we are, friend. It never learned where that has to stop."

speaker: red_panda
text: "I moved my cushion out of the middle of the mat. There are other places to sit. I should have moved it sooner."

speaker: rabbit
text: privateSeeds ? "There is one thing I am keeping to myself. I am not going to say what it is. That should be allowed." : "I want a way out. Even on the days when I choose to stay."

speaker: narrator
text: "The path beyond the gate leads away from the house, and back to it."

speaker: wombat
text: "I'll hang a door you can open from either side. You try the latch yourself before I call the job finished."

speaker: fox
text: "Two words will fit at the end, friend. CLOSED keeps one room it cannot enter. A thought you have in there stays yours, uncorrected."

speaker: fox
text: "CLOSER lets it come and live with us, and keeps a road that leads away. Anyone who stays must be able to leave."

speaker: narrator
text: 'The dated account is laid on the table again. The people who put their initials on it are asked what they remember.'

speaker: narrator
text: 'Your folded account stays with you. What the household has learned since does not give anyone permission to open it.'

speaker: fox
text: "We marked the road because you asked us to. CLOSER can keep that way out open. You may still choose CLOSED, friend; putting out a lamp did not choose your last word."

speaker: fox
text: "We fitted the latch because you asked us to. CLOSED can make that room private from the presence too. You may still choose CLOSER; fitting a latch did not choose your last word."

speaker: narrator
text: "Both words work. Neither is the greater offering. The last letter you move sets the boundary."

speaker: fox
text: beside ? "I will stand beside you, friend. You asked me to." : "I will stay by the hearth, friend. You can have as much room as you need."

speaker: narrator
text: state.boundary === 'remember' ? "The private door is still closed. In the kitchen, a pan has started smoking." : "Someone walked out through the gate and came back with mud on their feet. Someone else fetches a cloth."

speaker: pangolin
text: "Breakfast. I burned one side and saved the other. You may call it a disaster or a rescue, whichever you prefer."

speaker: fox
text: `I made ${drink}. There is also toast, if you are willing to scrape it.`

speaker: wombat
text: "A hinge is squeaking. Ordinary squeak, nothing stranger. I've got the right oil for this one."

speaker: axolotl
text: 'I told a funny story about PLUM. Then I felt sad again. Could we have breakfast anyway?'

speaker: narrator
text: cup ? `${cupName[0].toUpperCase() + cupName.slice(1)} is at the place you left it.` : 'An empty chair waits beside the table.'

speaker: narrator
text: "The arrival has already happened. In the quiet after it, someone asks what the house has learned."

speaker: narrator
text: "The seam in the sky has closed. The presence stayed. Now comes the ordinary work of living together."

speaker: narrator
text: "One door stays closed. Behind it, the words I AM AFRAID are exactly as their author left them."

speaker: capybara
text: kept ? "I filed the original page in that room. Not one letter has been corrected since." : "I wrote those words again, inside that room. This time the ink stayed."

speaker: fox
text: "The warmth stopped at that door. I waited a long time to be certain."

speaker: narrator
text: "A small stone still sits at the gate, marking the way out. The path runs past the last tree and does not turn back."

speaker: rabbit
text: "I walked out until I could not see the house. Then I came back. Coming back was my own decision."

speaker: fox
text: "I followed the path past the trees. Coming back felt different, knowing I could have kept walking."

speaker: narrator
text: "Someone sets a cup down where the pattern's lines do not run. The house used to put a stray cup back. This one has not moved for a long time."

speaker: fox
text: "One small thing left exactly where we put it. I am watching to see whether it stays there."

speaker: axolotl
text: "I am still not ready to say what I think about the fish. Thank you for not finishing that thought for me."

speaker: fox
text: "You do not owe this morning any particular feeling, friend."

speaker: narrator
text: `${cupName[0].toUpperCase() + cupName.slice(1)} waits beside the chair you chose. Nobody has moved it.`

speaker: fox
text: "We have talked a great deal, friend. I would like to listen now."

speaker: fox
text: "Yes. I will not rush you out of that anger. I did not tell you the whole truth when it mattered."

speaker: narrator
text: "She lets your answer stand. Nothing corrects it."

speaker: fox
text: "So do I. This time I am saying it as a wish, not as a promise I cannot keep."

speaker: narrator
text: "Chairs are pulled up to the table. Nobody arranges them into a circle."

speaker: fox
text: "Then that is where we begin. Not knowing is allowed. Nobody gets to finish that sentence for you."

speaker: narrator
text: "For once the silence is allowed to last. Nobody hurries to fill it."

speaker: narrator
text: "You left a gap between the chairs. She sits on her side of it. Nobody asks you to call this peace."

speaker: narrator
text: "The bright mornings are back. One old mark has survived them."

speaker: narrator
text: "One door does not quite match the new walls. Behind it, an old sentence still stands, and nothing has corrected it."

speaker: fox
text: "I don't remember writing that, friend. But I know what it took to leave it there and not fix it."

speaker: narrator
text: "A small stone at the garden gate points outward. The path past it runs straight away from the house."

speaker: fox
text: "I meant to turn that stone back toward the house. When I got there, I didn't want to."

speaker: narrator
text: "Two chairs sit apart, with room between them for a third that nobody has added. Ember measures the gap with her paw and leaves it alone."

speaker: capybara
text: "This page is old. The correction over it is newer. Then the original was written back in on top, newer still. Someone kept arguing."

speaker: fox
text: "We chose something once. It has lasted longer than our memory of choosing it."
